uncited: **Constraint Injection:** Unlike vanilla 3DGS which minimizes photometric loss $\mathcal{L}_{photo}$ alone, these methods add regularization terms or structural constraints.
For example, [GaussianBody](9209-gaussianbody.md) adds a physical prior loss $\mathcal{L}_{phys}$, while [SplattingAvatar](9556-splattingavatar.md) enforces mesh adherence.

**Representation Modification:** The Gaussian attributes or their initialization are modified to fit the domain. [GauHuman](9198-gauhuman.md) redesigns densification primitives; [SplattingAvatar](9556-splattingavatar.md) embeds Gaussians in mesh tangent space with trainable embeddings; [Inpainting for Displaced Objects](9523-inpainting-for-displaced-objects.md) modifies the kernel set by removing and reinitializing specific subsets.

**Specialized Initialization:** Standard SfM initialization is often replaced or augmented. [GaussianBody](9209-gaussianbody.md) initializes in canonical space based on parametric models; [SplattingAvatar](9556-splattingavatar.md) initializes one Gaussian per mesh triangle.

However, dynamic scenes, specific geometric constraints, and occlusion handling require specialized adaptations. [GauHuman](9198-gauhuman.md) and [GaussianBody](9209-gaussianbody.md) address the long-standing problem of dynamic human avatars from monocular video, where depth ambiguity leads to artifacts in clothing and body shape. [Inpainting for Displaced Objects](9523-inpainting-for-displaced-objects.md) addresses the specific failure mode of 3DGS when objects move, exposing unseen background. [SplattingAvatar](9556-splattingavatar.md) integrates 3DGS with parametric meshes (FLAME) to provide stable, controllable avatars.
